before_review.assessment: SOURCE 1–2 establish the same elongated building through its zigzag ramp end, projecting two-level glazed perimeter and curved roof. SOURCE 3 shows recessed lower glazing and exposed columns beneath projecting walkways; SOURCE 4 shows the timber roof underside, open interior and spiral stair. SOURCE 5–8 provide sections, plans and assembly diagrams showing the retained frame, added roof storey and outer buffer zone. CURRENT contains these broad exterior systems, but its roof-to-enclosure proportions differ visibly. The ramp-end view also shows unresolved landing connections. Repeated uncut obliques do not verify the source interior, floor voids or stair arrangement. No confirmed dimensions are supplied; screenshots cannot establish actual joint connectivity or hidden geometry.

issues.problem: In SOURCE 1–2, the roof’s lowest central edge remains appreciably above the horizontal outer enclosure top, leaving a visible band of upper-storey glazing. In CURRENT 15, that central edge nearly meets the enclosure top, compressing this defining glazed band. The unequal high ends also appear reversed relative to SOURCE 1; camera handedness remains uncertain.
issues.action: Locally adjust the roof profile and corresponding upper glazing/support heights to restore the source-backed central clearance. Establish matching ramp-end orientation before assigning the higher roof edge; retain the existing lower building during this correction.

issues.problem: CURRENT 15 shows the upper diagonal ramp/rail assembly extending beyond the right enclosure edge without a clearly resolved landing connection. SOURCE 1–2 show ramp flights terminating at identifiable perimeter landings. Dense overlapping lines in CURRENT obscure whether these are connected joints or passing intersections.
issues.action: Review the ramp-end landing closeups against the source, then locally trim or connect only confirmed overshooting ramp and rail ends. Verify deck-to-landing contact and continuous guarding; do not treat projected overlap as a completed joint.

keep: The straight horizontal top edge of the outer glazed enclosure, separate from the curved roof.
The existing roof’s smooth concave curvature; retain that character while correcting its vertical profile.

after_review.assessment: Sources 1–2 establish the same elongated building through its curved roof, projecting glazed upper enclosure and zigzag ramps at the short end. Source 3 shows the recessed entrance and open grated gallery; source 4 shows the timber ceiling, circular floor openings, spiral stair and double-height lower workspace. Sources 5–8 corroborate the concrete frame, timber upper addition, perimeter buffer zone and unequal internal floor extents. CURRENT captures these broad systems, but the ramp direction, internal void configuration and gallery construction differ visibly. Exact dimensions are not supplied. Images 22–25 repeat uncut exterior views and cannot verify the source sections; screenshots also cannot establish concealed joints.

issues.problem: SOURCE 1–2 shows the lowest ramp descending toward the right, with alternating flights above. CURRENT 15–16 descends toward the left and reverses that defining end composition; the upper flight also projects beyond the enclosure without a clearly resolved landing connection.
issues.action: Locally correct the ramp flights’ direction and landing positions using the shared end-view landmarks. Connect each flight to its intended floor or gallery with continuous walking surfaces and guards; verify clearances at the glazed enclosure.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4–5 shows a substantial double-height workspace beside a partial intermediate floor. CURRENT 21 instead shows closely stacked horizontal beams and floor surfaces across that region, substantially reducing the observed vertical opening. CURRENT 20 also leaves a circular floor opening unguarded, unlike the source’s circular mesh guards.
issues.action: Correct only the intermediate floor extent and associated beams around the source-backed double-height void. Align the spiral stair with the actual floor openings and landings, and guard the exposed circular opening.

issues.problem: SOURCE 3 shows a light, open gallery with visible transverse steel beams and translucent/open grating overhead. CURRENT 19 replaces this with a broad opaque grey soffit and deep continuous edge, obscuring the source’s structural rhythm and openness.
issues.action: Locally revise the gallery deck, soffit and edge assembly to expose the observed beam-and-grating construction. Check inclined support endpoints against actual structural members rather than accepting apparent screen-space contact.

keep: The visible short-end roof edge’s concave profile, including its higher right endpoint in the matched end view.
The recessed ground-level column line beneath the projecting gallery.

before_review.assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building: a recessed lower frame, a projecting two-storey glazed buffer enclosure, perimeter decks, three alternating end-ramp flights, and a curved timber roof with unequal raised edges. Exterior photographs, the aerial drawing and physical-model views share these landmarks. Interior panels show the curved timber soffit, exposed frame and spiral circulation; plans and sections show floor openings and differing internal floor extents. CURRENT retains the recognizable exterior arrangement, but the roof trough sits too close to the enclosure’s top edge, and ramp terminations need correction or closer verification. No user-confirmed dimensions are supplied. These uncut exterior views cannot establish internal fidelity or prove physical connections; dark outlines alone do not establish incorrect materials.

issues.problem: SOURCE end views show a substantial glazed zone between the roof trough and the horizontal buffer-enclosure roofline. In CURRENT image 15, the trough nearly touches that roofline, compressing the defining upper-storey silhouette.
issues.action: Raise the central portion of the curved roof and adjust its adjoining glazing/support heights locally to restore the source-visible clearance. Preserve the right-higher edge relationship; do not protect the entire existing roof profile.

issues.problem: CURRENT image 15 shows the upper ramp/rail extending beyond the right enclosure edge and broad projecting pieces at the flight ends. SOURCE physical-model views show flights resolving into perimeter decks and defined landings. The current overlaps do not demonstrate continuous walking surfaces or correctly terminated rails.
issues.action: Locally align flight endpoints with their receiving decks, trim unsupported overruns, and resolve landing surfaces and rail returns. Verify the joints in close views before accepting them; preserve correctly positioned flight portions.

keep: Right roof edge higher than the left in the matched ramp-end orientation.
Alternating slopes of the three exterior ramp flights.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE panels show one elongated building with a recessed lower frame, projecting two-level glazed buffer, exterior ramps, a raised concave timber roof, partial intermediate floors and circular stair/opening features. Exterior perspectives, interior views, plans, sections and exploded diagrams share these landmarks. CURRENT captures the broad massing but differs in ramp routing, interior floor configuration and opening assemblies. No confirmed dimensions are supplied. CURRENT exterior “section” views and roof-covered plans cannot verify hidden construction or concealed joints.

issues.problem: SOURCE 1–2 show successive visible ramp flights descending toward the same side beneath the asymmetric roof landmark. CURRENT 15/22 instead places alternating diagonal flights across the exposed end, changing the defining circulation elevation.
issues.action: Locally reroute the affected flights and return landings using the source end views and plans together; connect each flight flush to its receiving deck and remove unsupported projecting tails.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4–5/7–8 show a substantial double-height interior beside a partial intermediate floor. CURRENT 17/19 shows repeated floor and beam bands across that region, making the interior read as uniformly stacked storeys.
issues.action: Correct the intermediate slab extent and associated beams to preserve the source double-height opening. Verify the resulting configuration with an actual section through the matching location.

issues.problem: SOURCE 4 shows circular floor openings enclosed by cylindrical mesh guards. CURRENT 18 has two visibly unguarded holes and a long gray strip crossing the floor and opening edges, with no corresponding source feature.
issues.action: Complete the guards around the source-backed openings and remove or resolve the crossing strip so floor edges, stair access and guards form coherent assemblies.

keep: Concave roof-edge profile with one side higher than the other.
Raised roof volume inset from the outer rectangular buffer enclosure.
Recessed lower columns beneath the projecting perimeter decks.

after_review.assessment: SOURCE exterior panels share a recessed rectangular core, two upper glazed buffer levels, three descending ramp runs at the short end, and an elevated concave roof with unequal edge heights. Ground-level panels show concrete columns and projecting steel walkway supports; interior panels show a pale timber ceiling, light floors and guarded circular openings. Plans and sections additionally establish internal partitions and double-height regions. CURRENT captures the principal roof profile and layered arrangement, but ramp extents, facade/guard assembly and exposed floor openings differ visibly. CURRENT exterior views cannot verify the source’s internal section arrangement or concealed joints; no numerical dimensions are confirmed by these images.

issues.problem: SOURCE images 1–2 place the upper ramp runs and landings largely within the outer glazed end’s width. CURRENT images 15–16 extend both upper runs and their return landings substantially beyond its corners, widening the circulation silhouette.
issues.action: Locally shorten and reposition the upper runs and landings to match the source’s inset endpoints, retaining their descending arrangement. Ensure each landing connects continuously to its corresponding perimeter walkway.

issues.problem: SOURCE images 1–3 show a fine, pale outer frame and mesh guards with visually distinct glazing behind. CURRENT images 16–17 instead read as repeated heavy dark horizontal rails; ramp guards are open bars, and the source’s mesh infill is absent.
issues.action: Correct the visible frame and guard sections and finishes, add the source-backed mesh infill, and preserve the separation between glazing, guards and walkway edges.

issues.problem: SOURCE image 4 shows circular floor openings enclosed by raised mesh guards. CURRENT image 18 exposes two circular openings with no surrounding guards; the distant guarded stair opening does not resolve these omissions.
issues.action: Add fitted circular mesh guards around the two exposed openings, connected to their floor rims, using the source’s slender pale construction.

keep: Concave roof end profile with one edge higher than the other.
Three descending ramp runs at the short end.
Recessed ground-level column line beneath the projecting perimeter walkway.
